name: User Registration and Login
author: Dew Technolab

sections.description:
Add front-end registration, login and profile forms to any page with a shortcode. Forms are submitted with AJAX, and the plugin’s CSS and JavaScript load only on pages that show a form, which keeps the rest of your site fast.

Registration follows your “Anyone can register” setting and works with CAPTCHA and anti-spam plugins that hook into WordPress registration. Email changes made in the profile form are confirmed from the new address before they take effect.

For Registration Form Shortcode : [dew_register_form]

For Login Form Shortcode : [dew_signin_form]

For Profile Page Shortcode : [dew_profile_form]

sections.installation:
Starting with User Registration and Login consists of just two steps: installing and setting up the shortcode. User Registration and Login is designed to work with your site’s specific needs, so don’t forget to go through the User Registration and Login configuration wizard as explained in the ‘after activation’ step!

INSTALL USER REGISTRATION FROM WITHIN WORDPRESS

  1. Visit the plugins page within your dashboard and select ‘Add New’;
  2. Search for ‘User Registration and Login’;
  3. Activate ‘User Registration and Login’ from your Plugins page;
  4. Go to ‘after activation’ below.

INSTALL USER REGISTRATION MANUALLY

  1. Upload the ‘user-registration-and-login’ folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory;
  2. Activate the ‘User Registration and Login’ Plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress;
  3. Go to ‘after activation’ below.

AFTER ACTIVATION

  1. You should see the Dew Settings submenu in Setting menu;
  2. Go through the Dew Settings and set up the plugin for your site;
  3. You’re done!
sections.faq:
Do I need to have coding skills to use the User Registration Plugin?

No, you don’t need any coding skills. Add one of the shortcodes above to a page, then choose the redirect pages under Settings > Dew Settings.

Why is my new email address not saved straight away?

When a user changes their email address in the profile form, the plugin sends a confirmation link to the new address, and the change is saved when they open it. This stops someone who gets into an account from quietly taking it over. Developers can turn this off with the dew_profile_confirm_email_change filter.

Does the plugin work with any WordPress themes?

Yes, the plugin is designed to work with any themes that have been coded following WordPress guidelines.

How can I access registered users data?

All the users registered via the registration forms and their data can be accessed from the Users menu in the WordPress Dashboard.

I can’t find a question similar to my issue; Where can I find support?

For more information please visit http://dewtechnolab.com and check out the blog section from User Registration and Login Plugin.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Fix: The login, registration and profile forms did not submit on WordPress 5.6 and later.
  • Fix: Passwords were changed before being saved, so some passwords (for example ones containing “<“, “%” or double spaces) could not be used to log in. The 10-character password limit is removed.
  • Fix: The Lost Password link pointed to a broken address.
  • Fix: With the login and registration forms on the same page, registration read the wrong fields.
  • Fix: Errors now show a clear message instead of leaving the form on “Sending user info, please wait…”.
  • Fix: The profile form no longer depends on the “Anyone can register” setting.
  • Fix: The stylesheet no longer changes inputs, selects and text areas outside the plugin’s forms.
  • Fix: Accented characters in first and last names are kept.
  • Fix: Users can log in with an email address that contains an apostrophe.
  • Security: Registration respects the “Anyone can register” setting, validates the email address and runs the standard WordPress registration checks used by CAPTCHA and anti-spam plugins.
  • Security: Email changes in the profile form are confirmed from the new address, and invalid addresses are rejected.
  • Security: Updated jQuery Validation to 1.22.1 and escaped all output.
  • New: The site admin receives the standard new-user notification email.
  • New: Logged-in visitors see an “already logged in” message instead of being redirected, and logged-out visitors on the profile page get a login link.
  • Tweak: CSS and JavaScript load only on pages that show a form.
  • Tweak: The text domain is now user-registration-and-login so WordPress.org translations load, and all text is translatable.
  • Tweak: The plugin’s settings are removed when the plugin is deleted. Registered users are kept.

1.0.3

  • Added compatibility with WordPress version 7.0.0.

1.0.2

  • Added compatibility with WordPress version 6.7.1.

1.0.1

  • Fix error

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
